article: What changes between an A&W Canada Mama Burger and Teen Burger?
Compare the two official portions by energy, protein and sodium, then check a weight-based calculation.
Canadian A&W official product pages, as served without sides or drinks.
copy: A&W Canada lists its 170 g Mama Burger at 400 kcal and 20 g protein. The 250 g Teen Burger is listed at 500 kcal and 27 g protein. For a whole burger, the Teen adds 100 kcal and 7 g protein. Much of that comparison reflects a larger listed portion.
Choose whether you are comparing a burger or a fixed weight

The Mama gives about 235 kcal per 100 g. The Teen gives about 200 kcal per 100 g. The whole-item and common-weight rankings therefore differ. These figures do not identify which individual ingredients explain the difference. The listed sodium also includes the full burger as served.
Log the complete burger once and add any sides or drinks separately.

article: How do Mary Brown’s Pop-ins and pulled chicken poutines compare?
Compare the named Canadian poutine orders against the plain Taters Poutine base.
Canadian Mary Brown’s July 2026 nutrition guide. All are published completed dishes.
copy: The official Canadian guide lists Taters Poutine with Pop-ins at 820 kcal and 36 g protein. The pulled chicken version is 869 kcal and 39.7 g protein. Those are assembled orders. They already include the named poutine base, so adding the plain Taters Poutine row would count it twice.
Reuse the completed order without adding the base again

The plain order is 726 kcal and 24.7 g protein as listed. Compared with that order, the two completed versions add 94 and 143 kcal respectively. These differences describe the published builds and do not automatically give stand-alone nutrition for every Pop-ins or pulled chicken portion.
Choose the named order and retain its source serving if you enter a custom food.

article: Does doubling a Booster Juice smoothie’s size always double the label?
Compare Strawberry Sunshine and Mango Hurricane in 355 mL and 710 mL Canadian servings.
Booster Juice September 2026 Canadian nutrition guide. Snack and regular published drinks.
copy: Booster Juice’s Canadian guide lists 355 mL Strawberry Sunshine at 210 kcal and 710 mL at 410 kcal. Doubling the smaller number would give 420 kcal. Mango Hurricane is listed at 180 and 360 kcal, which does double across the same volumes.
Use the published size instead of predicting it

The protein figures show another limitation. The snack Mango Hurricane lists 2 g and the regular lists 3 g. These are published rounded entries. The figures do not give a reason to invent a new recipe or exact unrounded value for either size. Use the printed number for the size ordered.
The table compares standard drinks and excludes any customization or add-in not included in the listed build.

article: How much sugar is in four medium Chick-fil-A Canada Sunjoy mixes?
Read the four distinct medium Canadian drinks and compare the effect of changing both halves.
Chick-fil-A Canada official nutrition guide, four medium 641 g Sunjoy listed drinks.
copy: Four medium Sunjoy mixes have the same listed serving weight in Chick-fil-A Canada’s table. Their total sugars range from 7 g for the unsweet tea and diet lemonade version to 57 g for sweet tea and regular lemonade. The mix name alone does not identify the two halves.
Log the full drink’s published recipe

Use the published row for the exact combination rather than building it from half of two whole drinks whose listed weights differ. The comparison uses total sugars. It does not identify the added-sugar amount or predict a customized split. These are Canadian menu values.
If you also recorded either component separately, check that you did not duplicate the finished drink.

article: What changes between a GYG chicken Quesadilla and Quesadilla Plus in Australia?
Compare whole mild grilled chicken builds by published weight, calories and protein.
GYG Australia March 2026 nutrition guide. Mild grilled chicken, standard Quesadilla and Quesadilla Plus portions.
copy: The Australian guide lists the mild grilled chicken Quesadilla at 458 kcal and 29.8 g protein. Quesadilla Plus is 538 kcal and 31.0 g protein. The larger build adds 81 g listed weight and 80 kcal, but just 1.2 g protein in this matched filling comparison.
Keep the two named builds separate

That does not mean a separately ordered addition has exactly those numbers. The difference comes from two complete published products. If you enter Quesadilla Plus as a finished item, avoid logging the standard Quesadilla as a second component. Different fillings can change the result.
Use the precise version and its source weight when comparing with a similarly named dish in another market.

article: Why do GYG’s Australian enchilada figures list specific locations?
Read a standard mild grilled chicken enchilada alongside a location-scoped cheese-and-queso entry.
GYG Australia March 2026 nutrition guide, standard and location-scoped mild grilled chicken enchiladas.
copy: The GYG guide lists a standard mild grilled chicken enchilada and a separate cheese-and-queso enchilada scoped to World Square, Penrith, Kennington and Bendigo. The standard row shows 1,120 kcal and 56.7 g protein. The location-scoped row shows 1,150 kcal and 59.2 g protein.
Make the location part of the record

The source’s location note is as important as the item name. It identifies the scope of the listed build in that edition. It is not a promise that every store sells the version, or that any named location’s menu remains unchanged. Use the local ordering description to match what you bought.
Compare the two finished portions, and record any measured customization separately only if it is outside the published build.

article: Does the thinner Domino’s Australia crust have fewer calories per slice and per gram?
Compare classic and Thin ’N’ Crispy Cheesy Garlic slices by the listed piece and by 100 g.
Domino’s Australia nutrition table, Cheesy Garlic with Crème Fraiche, Classic and Thin N Crispy, one-eighth each.
copy: One classic slice of Australia’s Cheesy Garlic with Crème Fraiche lists 125 kcal. The Thin ’N’ Crispy slice lists 110 kcal. But the listed weights are 46 g and 29 g respectively. Per 100 g the comparison reverses, to roughly 272 kcal for classic and 379 kcal for thin.
Keep slice weight beside the calorie count

Both guides describe a slice of eight. That lets you compare pieces from the stated pies. A common-weight comparison answers a different question, especially if you serve more than one of the lighter pieces. It also cannot isolate what the crust alone contributes.
Use the actual pieces served or the measured edible weight. Keep any dip or extra topping separate when it is not in the selected entry.
table: Cheesy Garlic with Crème Fraiche, Australia

article: Why do two Domino’s Australia Cheesy Garlic crusts list 125 calories but different sodium?
Compare the classic and gluten-free source rows, keeping the actual slice size in view.
Domino’s Australia nutrition table for Cheesy Garlic with Crème Fraiche. One named slice of eight. No allergy suitability implication.
copy: Domino’s Australia lists both the classic and gluten-free Cheesy Garlic with Crème Fraiche slice at 125 kcal. The gluten-free entry weighs 42 g and lists 245 mg sodium. The classic entry weighs 46 g and lists 216 mg sodium. The label tie is for one field only.
Read the other fields even if calories match

Two slices of either give 250 kcal from the published rounded figures. Their sodium totals are about 490 and 432 mg respectively. Use the matching dish and crust when logging. A nutrient table does not determine whether a prepared product meets a particular allergy or cross-contact requirement.
For any dietary safety question, check the restaurant’s separate current allergen information and procedures.

article: Is KFC UK large gravy just two regular servings?
Compare both published gravy sizes before dividing a pot or adding it to an order.
KFC UK official nutrition guide. Sodium shown as the data’s sodium equivalent where reported as salt.
copy: KFC’s UK guide lists regular gravy at 73 kcal and large gravy at 166 kcal. Two regular amounts would total 146 kcal. If you share one large gravy equally with another person, half its listed value is about 83 kcal per person.
Scale the pot that you bought

The same difference appears in the sodium comparison. A half share of the large listing is about 560 mg sodium equivalent, compared with about 480 mg for a regular pot. The source values do not identify what was left behind, and a split only works when the shares are actually equal.
If a meal already includes gravy in its published total, check its scope before recording another pot.

article: Is a large KFC UK coleslaw the same as two regular portions?
Compare two separate published side sizes for calories and sodium rather than assuming the multiplier is exact.
KFC UK official nutrition guide. UK sodium is expressed on the source’s salt-equivalent basis where relevant.
copy: One UK regular coleslaw lists 150 kcal and one large lists 299 kcal. The energy is nearly identical to two regular portions. But the sodium conversion differs slightly. The large is about 440 mg sodium equivalent and two regular portions total around 456 mg.
Compare the two values for the serving you ordered

If a table rounds salt on declared servings, multiplying the printed line can differ from the number used for another named portion. Do not infer the exact reason for this difference without more information about the recipe and serving. For one large order, record the large row itself.
When sharing, split the one actual portion by the amount eaten. The comparison covers the side alone.

article: Is a large Subway New Zealand Italian Meatball salad a double regular?
Compare two complete New Zealand salad portions and calculate an equal split of the large order.
Subway New Zealand May 2026 nutrition guide, regular and large Italian Meatball salad. Values are source-specific.
copy: Subway New Zealand’s guide lists the regular Italian Meatball salad at 299 kcal and 16.2 g protein. The larger named salad lists 585 kcal and 31.5 g protein. Those energy and protein numbers are near double, but the listed food weight is 580 g versus 340 g.
Compare the most relevant size

If you ate half the large salad and the ingredients were distributed evenly, you could estimate around 293 kcal and 15.8 g protein. Use the large row for that calculation. Using a complete regular salad as a proxy would assume the meatball and salad proportions are identical, which the document does not establish.
Custom dressings or toppings need the portion they actually add. These are New Zealand values.

article: What changes between Subway NZ’s mini and six-inch Veggie Delite with avocado?
Compare the two complete New Zealand sandwiches, keeping their serving weights and the avocado build visible.
Subway New Zealand May 2026 nutrition guide, Veggie Delite with Avo mini and six-inch.
copy: Subway New Zealand lists its Veggie Delite with Avo mini at 183 kcal and 6.4 g protein for 130 g. The six-inch entry lists 359 kcal and 15 g protein for 216 g. The weight rises by about two-thirds, while energy roughly doubles.
Read the exact build name and portion together

Use the chart’s complete build from the actual size you ordered instead of estimating the six-inch by multiplying a mini entry. The precise ingredients and amounts can differ by build, and the guide does not isolate which part explains that difference. A wrap or salad has its own line.
If you added or removed an item, check whether there is a matching local source value before calculating the adjustment.
